newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics to bundle Juno free e-mail.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics to bundle Juno free e-mail.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp. and Juno Online Services LP said Tuesday that they had reached a deal under which U.S. Robotics will include Juno's free, advertising-supported electronic mail service with all Sportster desktop modems.

The companies said the Juno service, which offers computer users a way to send e-mail messages over the Internet for free, will be delivered as part of a package of software that comes with the U.S Robotics modems.
Sportster is the world's best-selling brand of personal computer modem for consumers.
Juno was created and financed by D.E. Shaw & Co LP, a New York investment bank that specializes in computer technology financing.
Juno said it has signed up more than 300,000 subscribers since the electronic mail service became available, making it the largest free service in the world.

Electronic mail services like Juno, and similar services such as Freemark Communications Inc.'s Freemark Mail, allow people to send and receive simple text messages for free over the Internet, the most popular use for such computer networks.

The Juno service derives revenues from advertisers who pay to have their ads displayed to subscribers, who pay no access fees or per-minute usage charges as a result. Juno also offers additional pay-as-you-go information service options.
